summary: Fix named-being/celestial rule contradiction, same-sentence repeat coref contradiction, temporal exemption for abstract-predicate content of saying verbs, entity status of list items/idioms in value slots, topic-noun conjunct headed by its relative verb, habitual-over-process for periodical nominals, existence verbs state, null-conceiver only when used, place postpositions, possessive pronoun no :possessor, 有/count-as lookup traps; trimmed redundant text for space.

edits.old: It is compared node by node with an expert gold annotation; check each graph and its document-level relations.
UMR 0.9, abridged, for Chinese and English at Stage 1 (numbered PropBank roles), with the names of the UMR release data.
A UMR has two levels.
- **Sentence level**: one rooted PENMAN graph per sentence (concepts, roles, attributes).
- **Document level**: temporal, modal and coreference relations between nodes, across sentences.
- Balanced parentheses; each variable defined once, starting with `s<N>`.
## 7. Checklist

Use the coarse values:
- participles and relative-clause verbs (*the man who left*: `(p / person :ARG0-of (l / leave-11))`);
- A named human is `individual-person`, not `person`. `person` stays for pronouns and unnamed people.
(*a tall man*: `:mod (t / tall)`)
Ordinals: `(o / ordinal-entity :value 2)`.
(*the meeting*, 探索 as a noun)
*he walks to work*,
Example: a periodical printed in some colour or format → `(y / 印刷-01 :manner (c / <colour word>) :aspect habitual)`.

Types as in AMR (`country`, `city`, `organization`, `company`, ...). A celestial body is `planet`/`star` + `:name`. Any named being, also a fictional character or alien, is `individual-person`; a common category noun before a name is the concept, with `:name` for the rest.
edits.new: Any named being (human, character, alien, mascot) is `individual-person`, never `person` or the category noun; a name of common words is still a name (one `:op` per word), and a category word written with it at first mention goes inside the name. 地球, 月球, 太阳 are names: `planet`/`star` + `:name`.

edits.old: - Within one sentence, coreference is a re-entrancy in the graph (one variable), not a `:coref` triple.
edits.new: - Within one sentence, only pronouns and unexpressed mentions are re-entrancies; a mention with its own noun (shortened name, repeated head noun) is a new node plus a `:same-entity` triple.

edits.anchor: The event under its `:ARG2` does get them.
edits.text: - An abstract predicate that is the content of a saying or thinking verb gets a modal parent but no temporal parent; its inner events are `(reporting-verb :overlap e)`.

edits.anchor: 等 / *etc.* closing a list is always its last `:opN`, not `:mod`.
edits.text: List-item activity nouns, and an idiom filling an abstract predicate's value slot, are plain entities (no sense, aspect or triples). If N has no outer role but a relative-clause verb, that verb heads the clause (and is the anchor) with N as its argument.

edits.old: is `habitual`, even with 了 or other completion marking.
edits.new: is `habitual`, even with 了 and also as an event nominal (overrides `process`). Another event nominal for an ongoing generic activity is `activity`.

edits.old: Possession, belonging, existence and knowing verbs stay `state` even with 了, 过, 曾经 or a duration modifier.
edits.new: Possession, belonging, existence, survival and knowing verbs stay `state` even with 了, 过, 曾经, a duration modifier or under *continue*.

edits.anchor: A conceiver that is not in the text is `null-conceiver`.
edits.text: Write `(author :full-affirmative null-conceiver)` only if `null-conceiver` is a parent in that sentence.
